task: narwhal#691: Make Alloy OTLP trace enrichment trustworthy so k8s.namespace.name (and other k8s.* attributes) are determined solely by the collector from the sender TCP connection IP, close the direct-to-Tempo ingest bypass via tempo-ingress-policy and ambient/waypoint opt-out, lower memory_limiter to 256MiB with 64MiB spike_limit, document Local/Grafana/exhaustion trade-offs, keep 08-2-monitoring.sh parity, and verify rendered config + NetworkPolicy in R373.

events.summary: Scope: gitops/charts/narwhal-apps/templates/{k8s-monitoring,prometheus-stack,tempo}.yaml, gitops/resources/network-policies.yaml, scripts/cluster/08-2-monitoring.sh, docs/common/{lessons-log,unified-observability-contract}.md, scripts/test/lib/check-trace-k8s-attributes.py (R373), scripts/test/regression-check-kakao.sh, and this eval trace. Excluded: portal/, new collector Deployments, .review/, and live cluster/VM mutations.

Initial PR #729 enabled k8s-monitoring 4.2.0 applicationObservability defaults (pod_association k8s.pod.ip -> k8s.pod.uid -> connection, no node filter, no memory_limiter). Orchestrator live check (2026-11-19) from a dev pod sending resource attribute k8s.namespace.name=chaos-testing stored chaos-testing in Tempo (1 trace; dev: 0) and was rolled back. In round 2, orchestrator live check (2026-11-19) from a dev pod posted an OTLP/HTTP span directly to tempo.monitoring.svc.cluster.local:4318 with k8s.namespace.name=chaos-testing -> HTTP 200 and Tempo stored it under chaos-testing, because monitoring had only an egress NetworkPolicy (monitoring-egress) and Tempo exposed OTLP/Jaeger/Zipkin/legacy ports to all cluster pods.

Disabled applicationObservability (enabled: false) and configured collectors.alloy-logs via extraConfig + includeDestinations: [tempo] + alloy.extraPorts (4317/4318) + service.internalTrafficPolicy: Local + service.labels.istio.io/use-waypoint: none in k8s-monitoring.yaml and 08-2-monitoring.sh: otelcol.receiver.otlp -> otelcol.processor.memory_limiter (check_interval=1s, limit=256MiB, spike_limit=64MiB -> 192MiB soft limit, leaving 256MiB headroom for podLogsViaLoki inside 512Mi) -> strip_client_k8s (error_mode=propagate, delete ^k8s[.] and service.namespace) -> k8sattributes (node=HOSTNAME, connection-only pod_association) -> tempo. Closed direct Tempo bypass by adding tempo-ingress-policy (monitoring) in gitops/resources/network-policies.yaml allowing TCP 4317+15008 only from alloy-logs pods and TCP 3200+15008 only from grafana/prometheus/narwhal-portal/tempo (denying 4318/Jaeger/Zipkin/legacy OTLP and excluding monitoring/waypoint), disabling OTLP/HTTP 4318 (tempo.receivers.otlp.protocols.http=null) and opting Service tempo out of waypoint (istio.io/use-waypoint: none) in tempo.yaml and 08-2-monitoring.sh. Kept Grafana routed via alloy-logs:4317, documented internalTrafficPolicy Local, collector exhaustion residual risk and separate-Deployment follow-up in unified-observability-contract.md and lessons-log.md, and extended R373 to pin the NetworkPolicy and config.
